events.desc: Penelope Pitstop: Well, hello there, everyone! Clara Bellingham, pleased as punch to meet y'all! What a positively magnificent old manor — dusty chandeliers, stern portraits, the whole nine yards! Now, before I go gallivantin' off lookin' for diamonds and whatnot, a proper lady always signs the guest book. Let's see what we've got here...

Oh my stars, what a gathering! Every one of these folks looks like they've got their own reasons for being here. But I believe the best in people, and I'm sure we'll all get along just splendidly. Now, that guest book might just be the first breadcrumb on the trail to the Doily Diamond!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Welcome, welcome to Doily Manor, esteemed guests! I am Pemberton, estate manager to the late Lord Doily — may his soul rest in eternal comfort. I do hope your journeys were not too arduous. If you'll permit me just one moment, I shall consult the guest book to ensure all arrivals are properly accounted for. One must maintain standards, after all!

So many witnesses... so many potential complications. But the real question burns in my mind like acid — where is Clara Bellingham? She is not among this gaggle of guests, which means she has a head start somewhere in this crumbling pile. I must find her before she finds the treasure. But first — the mask. Always the mask. Pemberton smiles. Pemberton serves. And Pemberton watches.

The Ant Hill Mob: Right lads, we've arrived! Doily Manor — very grand, very dusty, very... ominous. Now listen up — has anyone seen Clara Bellingham? Because she's not in this room and that makes me EXTREMELY nervous. Our one job — our ONE job — is to keep that girl safe, and she's already gone missing on us! Well, not missing exactly, she's probably just in another room, but STILL. We need to find her. But first — let me have a look around this foyer. That chandelier up there looks like it could come down any second, and if Clara walks under it... well, I don't even want to think about it!

I don't like the look of this place one bit. And that Sneekly character — there's something about him that puts my teeth on edge. Can't say what exactly, but my gut's churning like a cement mixer. Still, can't go accusing people without proof. Mum always said, 'Give people the benefit of the doubt, even when your doubt is screaming at you.' Right now my doubt is screaming quite loud indeed.

Dick Dastardly: Ladies and gentlemen! How FORTUITOUS that I should arrive at this very moment! You see, I happen to be an expert in Victorian manor architecture — published three papers on the subject, naturally — and I can tell you with ABSOLUTE CERTAINTY that these old estates always kept their valuables in the kitchen cellars. Something about the cold stone preserving gold, you understand. The wood-burning stove in there? Classic concealment device. I'd wager my CONSIDERABLE reputation that there's a hidden vault beneath it. You'd all better hurry — first come, first served, as they say!

Heh heh heh! That ought to send the lot of them scrambling into the kitchen like rats after cheese. Meanwhile, I shall slip into the library and examine that rather INTRIGUING inscription on the mantelpiece. Reginald Foxworth doesn't share treasure — Reginald Foxworth TAKES treasure. And if anyone asks why I'm not heading to the kitchen myself? Why, I'm simply being GENEROUS, letting them have first crack! The perfect gentleman villain, that's me.

Peter Perfect: James Hartwell has arrived at Doily Manor! *adjusts cravat with practiced precision* What a magnificent foyer — dusty, yes, but one can see the grandeur beneath the neglect. Now then, before I embark upon my mission — and I do have a most elaborate plan forming already — a true gentleman always signs the guest book. One must observe the proprieties, even in the pursuit of treasure and the protection of the fair Clara Bellingham!

Clara is not here. My heart aches with every moment I cannot demonstrate my gallantry to her. But patience, James — patience and preparation! I shall examine this guest book, survey the exits, catalogue potential dangers — that chandelier, for instance, is a death trap waiting to happen — and formulate a seventeen-step plan before proceeding. A lesser man would rush in. James Hartwell prepares.
Penelope Pitstop examined the guest-book.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the guest-book.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the null.
Dick Dastardly examined the guest-book.
Peter Perfect examined the guest-book.

Penelope Pitstop: Well now, that guest book was charmin' but not exactly brimmin' with clues, bless its heart! But did y'all hear that? The library has a carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription! An inscription, sugar — that's practically a riddle wrapped in a mystery tied up with a bow! And if there's one thing Clara Bellingham knows, it's riddles. I am positively THRILLED to go investigate! Dick, honey, your kitchen theory sounds fascinatin' — you go right ahead and check that out. I just have a feelin' about this library. Call it feminine intuition! Anyone who wants to join me for a little literary detective work is more than welcome!

Oh, I just get the most wonderful tingly feeling when there's an inscription to decipher! The Doily Diamond could be hiding behind any clever wordplay in this old manor. And I do notice Dick Dastardly was awfully insistent about everyone heading to the kitchen — but I'm sure he's just being helpful in his own boisterous way. No sense in being suspicious of perfectly friendly treasure hunters!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

Oh, how PERFECTLY it falls into place! I, Vincent Marsh, shall lead the lamb directly to the slaughter — wrapped in Pemberton's impeccable hospitality, of course. The library! With its towering bookshelves that could so easily topple, its heavy stone mantelpiece, its dust-choked isolation from prying eyes. Once I separate Clara from that meddlesome Ant Hill Mob, the possibilities are ENDLESS. But patience, Vincent — patience! The scheme must be ELABORATE. The trap must be THEATRICAL. Anything less would be beneath me. First, earn her trust. Then, spring the trap. It's almost too easy... which means it won't be. It never is. But oh, how I RELISH the challenge!

The Ant Hill Mob: Wait — Clara! You've been here the whole time! I nearly wore me legs down to stumps worrying about you, and you're right here signing guest books like it's a garden party! Right, well, NOBODY PANIC, but I am now conducting a FULL SAFETY AUDIT of this entrance hall. Starting with this coat rack here, which is wobbling about like it's had three pints. If that thing falls on Clara, I will NEVER forgive myself. Stand back everyone — let a professional handle this.

The lads think I'm overreacting, but you mark my words — it's always the innocent-looking things that get you. A wobbly coat rack today, a collapsed staircase tomorrow. And that Sneekly fellow keeps glancing at Clara when he thinks nobody's watching. I don't like it. I don't like it one bit. But Mum said give people the benefit of the doubt, so I'll keep my gob shut... for now.

Dick Dastardly: Well, I must say, what a THOROUGHLY fascinating guest book! Full of clues, absolutely BURSTING with them — all pointing to the kitchen, naturally. I do believe Lord Doily himself wrote 'treasure beneath the stove' in the margins! You should ALL go and investigate immediately. As for me, I shall just... stretch my legs in the library. Bit of light reading, you know. Nothing of interest in there — just dusty old books. Terribly DULL place, the library. Wouldn't recommend it to ANYONE.

Heh heh heh! Could I BE any more brilliantly devious? 'Nothing of interest in the library' — oh, Reginald, you magnificent scoundrel! They'll be crawling through kitchen cupboards while I decipher that mantelpiece inscription and find the treasure ALL BY MYSELF. Medal, glory, and riches — the holy trinity of a Foxworth victory! Now, quick — to the library before anyone gets suspicious about why I'm being SO insistent about the kitchen!
Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

My heart is SOARING! She is here — Clara Bellingham herself, radiant even amid the dust and gloom of this foyer! I must confess my hands are trembling slightly. But I shall channel this nervous energy into thoroughness. The library shall be swept, catalogued, and rendered completely safe before she sets one dainty foot across its threshold. And if there happen to be treasure clues hidden among those bookshelves... well, discovering riches while protecting the woman I admire would be rather impressive, wouldn't it? James Hartwell — gallant, brave, and just a little bit magnificent.
Penelope Pitstop walked into the library.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) walked into the library.
The Ant Hill Mob examined the coat-rack.
Dick Dastardly walked into the library.
Peter Perfect walked into the library.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, would you just LOOK at this magnificent mantelpiece! Oh, I am absolutely DELIGHTED — an inscription, just like I hoped! Now let me see here... 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish.' Why, sugar, that's a riddle! And Clara Bellingham LIVES for riddles! Now let me think... cities without houses, forests without trees, water without fish... why, that's a MAP! A map has all those things drawn on it without any of the real things! Oh, I just KNEW coming to the library was the right call! Let's see what happens when I give this old mantelpiece my answer!

I do notice that Dick Dastardly told everyone the library was 'terribly dull' and tried to send us all to the kitchen — and yet here HE is, right behind me! But I'm sure he just changed his mind. People are allowed to change their minds, after all!
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

Misdirection — the oldest trick in the book, and yet it NEVER fails! Send them all chasing a globe in the conservatory while I, Vincent Marsh, return under cover of darkness to claim the MAP that this riddle so obviously points to. The bookshelves, though — did you notice how I mentioned them being 'precariously placed'? I'm planting seeds, my friends. Seeds of a most ELABORATE and THEATRICAL demise. One good push and an entire wall of leather-bound volumes comes crashing down upon poor, unsuspecting Clara. But not yet. Not with witnesses. Patience is a virtue I possess in ABUNDANCE... when the prize is worth it.

The Ant Hill Mob: OI! LADS! Everyone's gone to the library without us! Clara's in there with — well, with EVERYONE, and we're out here inspecting furniture like a bunch of antiques dealers! The coat rack is wobbly, yes, NOTED, DOCUMENTED, we'll come back to it. But Clara is in the LIBRARY and I've got a funny feeling in me stomach — not the pie from earlier, a PROPER funny feeling. The kind me Mum used to say means trouble's brewing. Come on, Muttley, Sergeant, Professor, Private — MOVE IT! We stick together and we stick to Clara like wallpaper! Nobody's getting between the Ant Hill Mob and our Clara, not on MY watch!

I've made a tactical error, haven't I? Got so wrapped up in the coat rack that I let Clara walk off into the library with Dastardly AND Sneekly. Two suspicious characters, one room, one Clara. That's bad arithmetic, that is. Sneekly was practically PURRING about escorting her — 'labyrinthine for the uninitiated,' he says. Who talks like that about a library? Someone who knows there's more to it than books, that's who. And Dastardly — telling everyone the library is 'dull' and they should go to the kitchen? Then HE goes to the library? Classic double-bluff! But I can't say nothing, can I? No proof. Just... feelings. Strong ones. Very strong ones. Right, shut up and move your legs.

Dick Dastardly: Well well WELL, what a DELIGHTFUL surprise to find you all here! I was just coming for a spot of light reading, as I said. But LOOK at this — do you see? Several of those books are upside down! That's OBVIOUSLY a code, a cipher, a hidden message! In my extensive experience as a decorated treasure hunter — yes, I have a medal right here to prove it — upside-down books ALWAYS indicate the primary hiding spot. You should ALL examine those bookshelves IMMEDIATELY. Every single one of you. Turn them right-side up, shake them out, read every page! The treasure is CERTAINLY hidden inside one of those volumes. Don't mind me — I'll just be over here... stretching my legs by the fireplace. Terribly stiff from all that walking, you understand. Nothing to see at the mantelpiece. Dreadfully BORING bit of stonework. Wouldn't waste your time on it!

Heh heh HEH! Oh, Reginald, you MAGNIFICENT rogue! Send them all scrambling through dusty books while I crack the riddle on the mantelpiece! The answer is a MAP, of course — any Foxworth worth his salt knows that one. Cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish — it's a MAP! And once I interact with that mantelpiece and speak the answer, it'll reveal the next clue — and the treasure will be MINE! All mine! Medal-worthy cunning, if I do say so myself!
Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

My heart is THUNDERING. I have just solved a riddle in front of Clara Bellingham with the ease of a man who solves riddles every morning before breakfast — which I absolutely do not, but she doesn't need to know that. If there truly is a map hidden here, finding it would combine intellectual prowess WITH treasure-hunting heroism. The complete package. James Hartwell, you magnificent specimen of gallantry.
Penelope Pitstop interacted with the mantelpiece.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) examined the bookshelves.
The Ant Hill Mob walked into the library.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.
Peter Perfect interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my STARS, did y'all see that? The answer is a MAP! A map has cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish — it's all drawn on but none of it is REAL! Peter, sugar, you got it too — we make quite the detective team, don't we? Now here's what I'm thinkin' — and stay with me because this is where it gets EXCITIN' — if the riddle's answer is a map, then there must BE a map somewhere in this very room! And what do we have right here? Floor-to-ceiling bookshelves crammed with dusty volumes, and some of them are UPSIDE DOWN! Dick, honey, you might have been onto somethin' with those books after all! A map could be tucked inside one of those turned-around volumes — it's the oldest trick in the book, pun very much intended! Sneekly, dear, you're already over there tidyin' up — have you found anything interestin' among those shelves?

I do find it just the teeniest bit curious that Dick Dastardly declared the library 'terribly dull' and tried to herd everyone to the kitchen, then followed me straight here and is now trying to shoo everyone toward the bookshelves while he lingers by the fireplace. But I'm sure there's a perfectly innocent explanation. Maybe he just really loves books!

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): Ah, how curious indeed! I've had a look at these bookshelves, and I must say, Lord Doily's filing system was — well, ECCENTRIC would be putting it kindly. Several volumes placed quite upside down, you see. Whether that's a code or simply the work of a man who shelved his books after too much port, I couldn't say. Do be careful near them, though — they're rather TOP-HEAVY, I'm afraid. One good nudge and the whole lot could come tumbling down. Lord Doily really ought to have had them bolted to the wall. Now then, Mr. Hartwell — did that old mantelpiece give up any of its secrets? I confess I've dusted that inscription a thousand times and never could make heads or tails of it myself!

TOP-HEAVY bookshelves that could come TUMBLING DOWN. Did you catch that? I'm practically writing the instruction manual for Clara's demise, and not a soul suspects a thing! But first — I MUST see what Perfect found at that mantelpiece. If there's a map hidden there, I need to know where it leads before anyone else. The treasure AND Clara's fate — both within my grasp, if only I can stay one step ahead of these bumbling do-gooders!

The Ant Hill Mob: WE'RE HERE! Nobody panic — well, nobody ELSE panic, I'VE been panicking enough for everyone! Clara! Miss Bellingham! Oh thank GOODNESS you're alright! We came as fast as we could — got a bit held up in the entrance hall, coat rack situation, don't ask — but we're HERE now and we ain't going NOWHERE! Now then — Mr. Sneekly, sir, did I hear you say those bookshelves are PRECARIOUS? Well you can't be tidying those on your own, can you? Health and safety! The lads and I will give you a hand — we're EXCELLENT with heavy things, aren't we lads? Clump, you take the left side, Dum-Dum, you take the right, and I'll — I'll supervise from the middle. Nobody's getting bonked on the head by a falling encyclopedia on OUR watch! Not while the Ant Hill Mob draws breath!

Something about Sneekly wanting to 'tidy' books he just called dangerous while Clara sits underneath them... I don't like it. I don't like it ONE BIT. But I'm not clever enough to explain WHY I don't like it. Best thing I can do is plant meself right between those shelves and Clara. If something falls, it falls on ME. That's the Brixton way.

Dick Dastardly: Ha HA! Did you all see that? I, Dick Dastardly — that is, Reginald Foxworth — just SOLVED the mantelpiece riddle! A MAP, naturally! I knew it INSTANTLY, of course. Worked it out in the entrance hall, actually — that's why I came straight here. Not because of what anyone ELSE said. Pure Foxworth intellect! Now then, whatever that mantelpiece has revealed belongs to ME by right of superior deduction. Stand ASIDE, everyone — let a decorated treasure hunter examine the results! I DO have a medal, you know!

Curses and DOUBLE curses! Peter Perfect got to the mantelpiece at practically the same moment I did! And Penelope blurted out the answer — MAP — before I could even open my magnificent mouth! But no matter — I interacted with it TOO, so whatever it revealed, I can claim credit. The key now is to see what it showed and grab whatever comes next before these bumbling do-gooders realize what's happening. Reginald Foxworth does NOT share treasure!
Peter Perfect spoke quietly with penelope-pitstop.

Did she see that? Please tell me she saw that. I touched the mantelpiece with the confidence of a man who has touched many mysterious mantlepieces — which I have NOT, but the important thing is the confidence. Now I simply must discover what the interaction revealed. If a secret map tumbles out while Clara watches, I may actually faint from the sheer perfection of this moment.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh Peter, sugar, you are just the SWEETEST thing — checking for hostile dust particles on my behalf! A twelve-step Library Protocol, imagine that! Now listen here, everybody — Peter's gone and activated that mantelpiece mechanism, which is just WONDERFUL, but I have a hunch about these upside-down books! See, the riddle answer was MAP, and in my experience, when someone deliberately turns books upside down on a shelf, it ain't because they were shelvin' after too much port — no offense, Sneekly dear. It's because those spines spell somethin' out, or one of 'em is a lever! I'm gonna try rearrangin' these turned-around volumes and see if they trigger anything. Ant Hill Mob, darlings, thank you SO much for steadyin' these shelves — y'all are absolute angels! Now hold tight while I give these topsy-turvy books a little... nudge!

I do declare, this is the most fun I've had since the county fair puzzle maze back in '09! Now, Dick tried to get everyone AWAY from the library, then rushed here himself and went straight for the mantelpiece — and now Peter's activated it. If there's a hidden compartment in that fireplace, I have a sneakin' suspicion Dick already knew about it. But Clara Bellingham doesn't point fingers — she just makes sure she's standin' in the right spot when the secret panel slides open! These upside-down books might be the REAL clue everyone's overlookin'.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) spoke quietly with peter-perfect.

Oh, this is EXQUISITE! While Perfect preens and Clara rummages through dusty books, I — Vincent Marsh — shall be the one to crack open that mantelpiece! Whatever map or clue lies within, it passes through MY hands first. And if I happen to palm a crucial piece, or read it before anyone else, or subtly MISDIRECT them about what it says — well, that's just good estate management, isn't it? The beauty of the Pemberton disguise is that NOBODY questions the butler knowing his way around the furniture. It's PERFECT. Now — let me see what Lord Doily's little puzzle box has been hiding all these years!

The Ant Hill Mob: RIGHT THEN! Nobody touch NOTHING! The lads and I have done a THOROUGH inspection of these bookshelves — thorough, I say — and there are MULTIPLE books what are upside down! Now, Miss Penelope's got a point — if the riddle answer is a MAP, then a map's GOT to be hidden in one of these wonky volumes! And since Mr. Sneekly has VERY KINDLY warned us that the shelves are top-heavy and precarious — thank you for that, Mr. Sneekly, very public-spirited of you — it only makes SENSE that the Ant Hill Mob handles the dangerous bit! We are TRAINED for this! Well, not TRAINED exactly, but we are EXPERIENCED in things falling on us! Clump, you hold that side steady! Dum-Dum, you hold THAT side steady! I'm going to carefully — VERY carefully — turn these upside-down books the right way round and see what falls out! Everyone STAND BACK! Especially you, Miss Bellingham — you stay RIGHT there in that chair where it's SAFE! If anyone's getting buried in an avalanche of Victorian literature, it's going to be ME!

I'm doing two things at once here, and I'm only clever enough to know ONE of them. Thing one: checking the upside-down books for the map, which is the obvious move. Thing two — and this is the IMPORTANT one — I'm putting meself between Clara and those shelves. If Sneekly was planning to 'accidentally' topple them onto her, well, NOW he'd be toppling them onto the entire Ant Hill Mob. And we're STURDY. Not bright, but sturdy. Let him try something NOW. Go on, Sneekly. I DARE you.

Dick Dastardly: Stand BACK, everyone! You're all fumbling about with dusty books like common librarians, but you're missing the OBVIOUS solution! The mantelpiece doesn't just want you to KNOW the answer — it wants you to GIVE it the answer! Watch and learn from a MASTER of riddle-solving! The answer is... well, it's certainly NOT a map. That would be far too simple. No no no — the REAL answer is... a GLOBE! Yes, a globe! Cities, forests, water — all on the surface but none of them real! Now, if everyone could kindly look the other way while I demonstrate my superior intellect to this mantelpiece...

Heh heh HEH! I'm telling them the answer is a GLOBE instead of a map — pure GENIUS! If they waste time looking for a globe while I secretly interact with the mantelpiece using the CORRECT answer, the treasure is MINE! Of course, the answer is obviously a map — I'm not an IDIOT. I just want everyone ELSE to be idiots. Now, let me interact with this mantelpiece properly before Peter Perfect muscles in with his perfect jawline and his perfect riddle-solving!

Peter Perfect: I say — the mantelpiece is a MAGNIFICENT piece of stonework, truly splendid craftsmanship, but I'm afraid it has yielded all it intends to for now. The riddle's answer is indeed a MAP, as Clara so brilliantly deduced — and I must say, Clara, your reasoning was absolutely IMPECCABLE. Now then! If the riddle tells us to seek a map, and we have before us an entire wall of books with several placed UPSIDE DOWN — well, that's practically a flashing neon arrow, isn't it? James Hartwell does not ignore flashing neon arrows! I shall conduct a thorough examination of these bookshelves. But first — everyone please stand back at least three paces. Mr. Sneekly has warned us they're top-heavy, and I will NOT have anyone crushed by a falling encyclopaedia. Especially not you, Clara. I shall position myself between you and the shelves as a precautionary measure. Safety FIRST, treasure second, glory... well, glory whenever it arrives, really.

Right then, James — the mantelpiece was a dead end, but Clara's bookshelf theory is INSPIRED. If I can find a hidden map among those upside-down volumes while simultaneously shielding her from any cascading literature, that would be the most heroically multitasking thing I've ever done. My heart is doing that fluttery thing again. Focus, man. FOCUS. Examine the shelves, find the map, look dashing. Three things. You can manage three things.
The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly) interacted with the mantelpiece.
Dick Dastardly interacted with the mantelpiece.
Peter Perfect examined the bookshelves.

Penelope Pitstop: Oh my stars, I nearly knocked myself silly tryin' to yank on those shelves like they were some kind of carnival lever! Clara Bellingham, where are your MANNERS — you don't just grab at antique bookshelves! You EXAMINE them, sugar, like a proper detective! Now let me get a closer look at these upside-down books — I just KNOW they're tryin' to tell us somethin'. Peter, darlin', you examine from your end and I'll take this side. And Dick, honey, the answer was MAP, not globe — but don't you fret, you were in the right neighborhood! Now then... let me see what these topsy-turvy spines are spellin' out...

I do notice Dick gave the WRONG answer to the mantelpiece on purpose — 'globe' instead of 'map.' Now why would a man who clearly knew about this library deliberately give a wrong answer? Unless he's tryin' to reset the mechanism or trigger somethin' different! But Clara doesn't assume the worst. Maybe he just genuinely thought it was a globe. Bless his heart.

The Hooded Claw (as Sneekly): If I may, ladies and gentlemen — as estate manager, I am rather familiar with Lord Doily's library. These shelves are organized according to his Lordship's own peculiar system — the upside-down volumes aren't accidents, they're MARKERS. Each one corresponds to a section of the manor. If the riddle's answer is indeed a map, then turning those books right-side-up in the correct ORDER should reveal Lord Doily's hidden cartography. But please, do be careful — these shelves haven't been properly maintained in years, and the upper sections are frightfully top-heavy. Perhaps everyone should stand well back while I attend to it? I DO know which volumes are load-bearing, so to speak.

Oh, the IRONY is absolutely DELICIOUS! Here I am, warning them about the danger of the shelves — the very danger I intend to WEAPONIZE! Once I'm the one at the bookshelf, one carefully chosen 'accident' — a support volume pulled at JUST the right angle — and an avalanche of leather-bound encyclopaedias comes crashing down on dear Clara Bellingham! And who could blame poor Pemberton? He WARNED them! He tried to keep everyone SAFE! The grief will be MAGNIFICENT. The performance of a LIFETIME!
The Ant Hill Mob spoke quietly with dick-dastardly.

Something's not right. Sneekly whispered to Peter — WHISPERED. In a library full of people. And now Dastardly's giving wrong answers to the mantelpiece like he's trying to break it on purpose. Are they working TOGETHER? I can't say nothing though, can I? No proof. Just this feeling in me gut. But I tell you what — if I'm the one pressing the mechanism, at least I KNOW nobody's rigged it. Well, I don't know that. But I'll find out the hard way, won't I? Better me than Clara.

Dick Dastardly: AH HA! You FOOLS! While you're all playing librarian with those dusty old books, I — Reginald Foxworth, MASTER treasure hunter — have noticed something you've ALL missed! There's a depression in the mantelpiece! A round, coin-shaped depression! And would you LOOK at that — I just so happen to have a medal of EXACTLY the right size! This medal, I'll have you know, was awarded to me by the Royal Geographic Society for outstanding cartographic achievements! Now watch as I insert it into this clearly obvious slot that NONE of you noticed because you were too busy alphabetising!

Heh heh HEH! The medal is completely fake, of course — I made it out of a chocolate coin wrapper and some old tin foil. But if there IS a slot in that mantelpiece, I'll look like a GENIUS. And if there ISN'T a slot... well, I'll just claim the mechanism is stuck and blame Sneekly's poor estate maintenance. Either way, I keep everyone watching ME instead of finding the actual clues in those bookshelves! Although... knowing MY luck, one of those upside-down books will fall on my head mid-demonstration. It's the Foxworth curse!

Peter Perfect: Thank you most kindly, Mr. Sneekly — your knowledge of Lord Doily's mechanisms is INVALUABLE, and I do appreciate you offering to work the mantelpiece. By all means, have at it, sir! But I believe Clara has cracked the REAL puzzle here. The riddle says MAP, and these upside-down books are no accident — they're a SIGNAL! Now then — Ant Hill Mob, you splendid fellows, keep those shelves braced! Clara, my dear, please remain in that reading chair where it's safe. James Hartwell is about to conduct what I can only describe as a SURGICAL extraction of literary clues. I shall work through these inverted volumes one by one — checking if their spines spell a word, if any of them functions as a lever mechanism, or if a map has been secreted between their pages. If the shelves so much as WOBBLE in Clara's direction, I shall interpose myself bodily. That is the Hartwell guarantee!

My hands are actually shaking with excitement. Clara called the upside-down books a SIGNAL — and she's RIGHT. If I can find a hidden map in these shelves while standing heroically between her and potential danger, this will be the single greatest moment of my life. Well, second greatest. The greatest will be when she looks at me with those eyes and says 'Peter, you wonderful man.' Which could happen ANY MOMENT NOW. Focus, James. Focus on the books. The glory will follow.
Penelope Pitstop examined the bookshelves.
The Ant Hill Mob interacted with the mantelpiece.

Penelope Pitstop: Well, sugar, those bookshelves are packed tighter than a debutante's dance card, but I couldn't quite make out which volumes are the special ones from just lookin'!
